item.description: Last year, Montgomery Academy volleyball narrowly missed a state tournament appearance after a heartbreaking loss in the second round. In 2026, that heartbreak was substituted with joy. Montgomery Academy claimed the Single A AHSAA South Regional championship in a 3-0 match win over Prattville Christian at the Multiplex at the Cramton Bowl on Thursday, Oct. 22. It's a significant contrast from where the Eagles were last season when the regional tournament ended. Now crowned as regional champions, Montgomery Academy will be on the hunt for a Blue Map under coach Jada Coleman in her first year as head coach of the Eagles. The Montgomery Advertiser breaks down what went right for Montgomery Academy in the championship game, and what it could mean for the state tournament. Montgomery Academy volleyball doesn't panic and never gives in Prattville Christian opened the first set with all the momentum over Montgomery Academy. The Panthers were slowly starting to overwhelm the Eagles in the early going, but not once did Montgomery Academy give in. Instead, the Eagles clawed their way back into the game behind a veteran presence and the aid from underclassmen. Seniors Rehmat Sidhu, Morgan Springer and Bennett Britt were able to get in rhythm and flip the momentum back in favor of Montgomery Academy. The level heads of its senior leadership give the Eagles a fighting chance, even when their backs are up against the wall. Montgomery Academy is methodical in its attack The Eagles don't always rely on one aspect of their game to prevail. Montgomery Academy is strategic in its approach when attacking for points. item.title: Tampa Bay Rays will have land & sea parades if they win World Series
item.description: The Tampa Bay Rays and Milwaukee Brewers begin their quest for World Series glory in Game 1 on October 23. Excitement is high in both cities as neither franchise has ever won a World Series. The city of Tampa has already begun parade planning in the event the Rays win the World Series. Multiple parades will honor the team if they bring the MLB championship home to Florida. The Florida (now Miami) Marlins are the only Sunshine State to win the World Series in 1997 and 2003. MORE: Rays choose surprise starter for Game 1 of World Series Tampa is planning another boat parade Oct 19, 2026; St. Petersburg, Florida, USA; Tampa Bay Rays third baseman Junior Caminero (13) celebrates after defeating the Cleveland Guardians in game six of the ALCS for the 2026 MLB Playoffs at Tropicana Field. Mandatory Credit: Pablo Robles-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) The prospect of another boat parade in Tampa is thrilling. Fans loved it when the Buccaneers had one in February, 2021. During that parade, a tipsy Tom Brady threw the Lombardi Trophy from his boat to the one behind him. NO PARADE WILL EVER TOP TOM BRADY GETTING DRUNK OUT OF HIS MIND AND THROWING THE LOMBARDI TROPHY FROM BOAT TO BOAT. 💀💀💀 LEGENDARY: pic.twitter.com/zunTS3XwtZ — MLFootball (@MLFootball) October 17, 2026 The Tampa Bay Lightning also had a boat parade in July 2021 celebrating their back-to-back Stanley Cup championships. (No parade was held in 2020 because of the COVID-19 pandemic.) LIGHTNING STRIKES TWICE: The Stanley Cup trophy went for a ride on a jet ski as the Tampa Bay Lightning celebrated back-to-back championships with a boat parade on Monday. pic.twitter.com/6xsDxXkcdp — CBS Evening News with Tony Dokoupil (@CBSEveningNews) July 12, 2021 MORE: Colin Cowherd calls out MLB & Junior Caminero in same rant St. Petersburg will have a traditional parade While the City of Tampa is planning its boat celebration, the adjoining city of St. Petersburg is planning a traditional parade with streets lined with festive fans. The Rays have a lot of work to do before potentially getting into parade mode. Games 1 and 2, October 23 and 24, are in Milwaukee. Floridians will get their first chance to cheer the Rays to victory in Game 3 on October 26. The Rays also host Games 4 and 5 on October 27 and 28 before moving back to Milwaukee for Games 6 and 7 as needed. All World Series games will be televised on FOX. — Enjoy free coverage of the top news & trending stories with The Big Lead Newsletter —

item.description: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - NOVEMBER 10: Caleb Williams #18 of the Chicago Bears passes the ball against the New England Patriots during the fourth quarter at Soldier Field on November 10, 2024 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images Could someone in the NFC North lose, please? Outside of the Detroit Lions, the last NFC North team to lose a non-division game was the Green Bay Packers back in Week 3. Since then, the Packers have won three straight, the Minnesota Vikings have yet to lose this season, and the Bears’ only two losses this season have come against NFC North teams. Thursday night provides a decent opportunity for an NFC North opponent to finally tally a non-division loss. The Chicago Bears are hosting the surging New England Patriots on Thursday night. Both teams share a 4-2 record through six games, but the Patriots appear to have righted the ship after a shaky 1-2 start. They beat the Bills, Raiders, and Jets in the last three weeks, with Drake Maye looking much better than his 2026 start. But Chicago also looked a lot better last week with Caleb Williams back behind center. They made quick work of the Atlanta Falcons, even if they almost let their three-touchdown lead slip away. This looks to be a surprisingly good matchup for a Thursday night game, and it obviously has big implications on the NFC North. So here’s a look at who our staff is picking for Thursday night. item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Colorado Avalanche were back on the ice Thursday for the first time since dropping two disappointing road games on back-to-back days. At 5-4-1 through their first 10 games, the Avs know they can be better. Consistency has been an issue early in the season, and while head coach Jared Bednar isn’t ready to panic, he wants to see his team get back to playing the way it should. He’s making that message clear to his players. “It’s not about the couple wins or couple losses. It’s just about how we want to play, what we want our game to look like,” Bednar said. “Just to summarize the season, we’ve had trouble putting together full 60 minutes. And slow starts or periods off. But when we’re good, we’re really good, and looking exactly the way I want us to look. “So you kind of start talking about getting a full 60 together and some of the things that we want to do, and then we go out and lay an egg for two games, right? It’s regroup time, go back to what we were trying to do before these two games and that’s play to our identity.” Kadri’s Workload Continues to Climb Nazem Kadri has taken on a heavier workload in recent games, playing more than 20 minutes in six consecutive contests after starting the season in the 17-minute range. Bednar credited Kadri for earning his ice time but acknowledged that Colorado’s 11-forward setup has also contributed to the increased workload. Kadri has primarily played on the wing on the second line while occasionally centering the fourth line, allowing the Avalanche to roll four lines without overtaxing Nathan MacKinnon . item.title: Chiefs Star Patrick Mahomes Recalls Being ‘Too Amped Up’ in Only Previous Seattle Game
item.description: Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs are having an excellent start to the season. They recently beat the Los Angeles Chargers with a score of 22-6. The team has won all 5 of their games so far, and are one of three teams to be still unbeaten. The Chiefs look very strong at the moment, and are being considered as a Super Bowl contender. Ahead of a crucial matchup, Mahomes had something to say. Patrick Mahomes remembers 2018 loss to Seahawks The Chiefs have managed to defeat all of their opponents so far, but will now face the Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field. The reigning Super Bowl champions are a formidable team, though they have a current record of 3 wins and 3 losses. However, Mahomes is not taking them lightly based on his previous matchup with the team at their home stadium. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Mahomes has only played the Seahawks at Lumen Field once in his career. It happened back in December 2018, with the Chiefs losing to the Seahawks with a score of 38-31. The quarterback performed well in that game, as he completed 23 passes for 273 yards and three touchdowns. The Chiefs last won at the stadium back in 2010. Ahead of the Seahawks game, Mahomes remembered the atmosphere at the 2018 loss in a recent press conference. He said , “I remember it being very loud, them having a lot of passion. I feel like I might have been a little too amped up kind of early in the game.” He added that it was a very important experience for him, “I think that’s something you learn from as you go throughout your career is like, you’ve got to be able to manage that.” Mahomes also talked about what qualities make the Seahawk an opponent to fear facing against. Patrick Mahomes addresses Seahawks defense In the same press conference, Mahomes talked about the current Seahawks team. He highlighted their defensive attributes. He said, “They’re good at every single level of the defense.” He added, “Defensive line, linebackers, secondary, everybody, and they have a great scheme. They’re going to make you earn it every single drive, and it’s not always going to be pretty, but you have to be consistent and not push it too far, but push it enough to make plays happen.” Head coach Andy Reid also mentioned that his counterpart Mike Macdonald runs one of the best defensive schemes in the league. Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs will now prepare as they face the Seattle Seahawks at their home. Ahead of a crucial matchup, Mahomes had something to say. Patrick Mahomes remembers 2018 loss to Seahawks The Chiefs have managed to defeat all of their opponents so far, but will now face the Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field. The reigning Super Bowl champions are a formidable team, though they have a current record of 3 wins and 3 losses. However, Mahomes is not taking them lightly based on his previous matchup with the team at their home stadium. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Mahomes has only played the Seahawks at Lumen Field once in his career. It happened back in December 2018, with the Chiefs losing to the Seahawks with a score of 38-31. The quarterback performed well in that game, as he completed 23 passes for 273 yards and three touchdowns. The Chiefs last won at the stadium back in 2010. Ahead of the Seahawks game, Mahomes remembered the atmosphere at the 2018 loss in a recent press conference. He said , “I remember it being very loud, them having a lot of passion. I feel like I might have been a little too amped up kind of early in the game.” He added that it was a very important experience for him, “I think that’s something you learn from as you go throughout your career is like, you’ve got to be able to manage that.” Mahomes also talked about what qualities make the Seahawk an opponent to fear facing against. Patrick Mahomes addresses Seahawks defense In the same press conference, Mahomes talked about the current Seahawks team. He highlighted their defensive attributes. He said, “They’re good at every single level of the defense.” He added, “Defensive line, linebackers, secondary, everybody, and they have a great scheme. They’re going to make you earn it every single drive, and it’s not always going to be pretty, but you have to be consistent and not push it too far, but push it enough to make plays happen.” Head coach Andy Reid also mentioned that his counterpart Mike Macdonald runs one of the best defensive schemes in the league. Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs will now prepare as they face the Seattle Seahawks at their home. The Dream’s first trip to the Finals in 2010 was in McCoughtry’s second WNBA season, when a young Atlanta team lost to an experienced Seattle team featuring Lauren Jackson, Swin Cash and Sue Bird. The Dream’s next two Finals defeats were at the hands of the Lynx, whose roster included five Olympians — Maya Moore, Sylvia Fowles, Seimone Augustus, Rebekkah Brunson and Lindsay Whalen. After sitting out the 2019 season in Atlanta with a torn ACL, she left and signed with the Las Vegas Aces for the 2020 season. And for Atlanta, they have a little more depth and history, but maybe it's their turn.” This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: 'Finally!' item.description: James Anderson first played for the Lancashire first team in 2001 [Getty Images] James Anderson will have options to extend his legendary playing career after being told he will not be given a new contract by Lancashire. A number of counties are keen to speak to the 44-year-old if he decides to continue playing next summer. Anderson will leave Old Trafford following Lancashire's decision to release him from the club for whom he first played professionally 25 years ago. Despite turning 45 in 2027, Anderson, who captained Lancashire last season, was planning on playing for another year before being told he will not be given a new deal. The exit from Lancashire leaves England's all-time leading wicket-taker with a decision over whether to retire or speak to other counties. It is understood clubs in both divisions of the County Championship would be interested in negotiating with Anderson and some have already reached out. Any move for Anderson would likely depend on the finances of the deal, the role he would be offered and the logistics of spending time away from his home in Cheshire. For a county, the signing of Anderson would represent an acquisition of unmatched quality on and off the field. Last summer, Anderson was Lancashire's County Championship player of the year, taking 50 wickets in Division Two. Only six other bowlers in the second tier managed more. It could also lead to the prospect of Anderson transitioning into a coaching role at a new county at the conclusion of his playing career. item.title: Freddy Peralta Starting Game 3 Could Be Ideal For These Two Reasons
item.description: Tampa Bay Rays pitcher Freddy Peralta The Tampa Bay Rays are starting Nick Martinez in Game 1 of the World Series, meaning Drew Rasmussen and Freddy Peralta will start Games 2 and 3. It's safe to assume Rasmussen will work on five days of rest for Game 2, and it will be Peralta starting at Tropicana Field for Game 3, working on six days of rest after making two starts and a relief outing in the American League Championship Series. This actually may work out best for the Rays, even though their two best starters will be pushed back a day. If Peralta pitched in Game 2, he would be on four days of rest and would have to deal with a ton of emotion that the other pitchers may not have to. It's a World Series game. The emotions will be high no matter what. However, for Peralta, pitching in Milwaukee comes with some added emotion. He spent the first eight years of his career with the Brewers and had nothing but great things to say about the city and organization when he met with reporters on Thursday. Peralta told reporters that pitching in Milwaukee would not bother him and that he would be unaffected by the added emotions of pitching at American Family Field, a venue he spent his entire career trying to bring a World Series to. Peralta's first outing at American Family Field not as a Brewer did not go so well. The Brewers tagged him for seven earned runs in 5 1/3 innings. The second reason that Peralta pitching in Game 3 may be ideal for the Rays is that all of his starts this postseason have come at home, and overall, he has pitched better at Tropicana Field than he has on the road with the Rays. item.title: Mizzou Men’s Golf places fifth at Abilene Christian Intercollegiate
item.description: Mizzou concluded its fall season with a 12-over team score, placing fifth out of nine teams at Halbert National Golf Club. The Tigers played Oct. 19-21 in Granbury, Texas, on the ultra-private golf course owned by biotech billionaire David Halbert. The team played best in the first round, starting with a 2-under team score before scoring 5-over and 9-over the next two rounds. Texas A&M dominated, taking the individual and team victories. The Aggies finished 17 strokes ahead of the second-place teams and the individual winner finished two strokes ahead of the second-place golfers. Individual performances Senior Veikka Viskari led the Tigers with a 1-under total to tie for 11th place. He shot 70-71-74. View this post on Instagram Freshman Antoni Hawkins followed in a tie for 15th place, shooting 73-73-70 to end even-par. Hawkins’ third-round 70 was the lowest of the team and marked the first tournament this season that he has scored progressively lower each round. “That was a really good final round,” said Mizzou head coach Glen Millican. “It was good to see him come out and make a nice move that last day.” Junior Trent Mierl shot 73-73-76 for a 6-over total to tie for 26th. Senior Brock Snyder tied for 35th with a 10-over total, shooting 70-79-77. Junior Paxton Maxwell shot 78-76-78 to finish 16-over. He tied for 41st. The course The brand-new 7,485-yard course, designed by acclaimed golf architect Tom Fazio, was enjoyed by the Mizzou players and Millican, but took patience and strategy. “If you drive it poorly, it’s definitely going to be tough because there’s penalizing bunkers, and then there’s some native area-like buffalo grass once you get outside of the rough,” Millican said. “The guys had to have good concentration all the way around.” Hole 8, a 200-yard par 3, was one of the toughest holes of the tournament, especially when the hole locations changed each round. According to Millican, it was difficult to get the ball close on the back part of the green. Every Mizzou golfer bogeyed hole 8 at least once, and it took an average of 0.43 strokes over par to complete for all players. There were also a handful of long par 4 holes, including 2, 4, 9 and 14, that required players to have good shots off the tee if they wanted to finish at- or under-par. “If you hit a good drive in the fairway, it was fine,” Millican said. “If you didn’t hit a really good tee shot, they played kind of long.” Hawkins did especially well on these holes during his third round, only bogeying hole 9. This, along with four birdies on the back nine holes, contributed to his lowest round of the tournament. The Tigers will take a well-deserved break from competition and return for the National Invitational Tournament starting Feb. 1.

item.title: Houston Comets, Tegna reach local TV deal to broadcast WNBA team's games on free over-the-air TV
item.description: Patrick Fertitta, Houston Rockets Alternate Governor and Director of Fertitta Entertainment answers questions during a press conference regarding the return of the WNBA's Houston Comets at the Toyota Center in Houston on Thursday, May 14, 2026. (Elizabeth Conley/Houston Chronicle) The Houston Comets' return is just about six months away and when they take the court, their games will be available for fans to watch on over-the-air TV for free. The Comets and Tegna announced a multi-year partnership Thursday that will make Houston CBS affiliate KHOU and also KTBU the local broadcast homes of Houston's WNBA team. Comets games also will be simulcast on Space City Home Network and streamed on the regional sports network's site SCHN+. As part of the partnership, KHOU (channel 11), which will simulcast select games with every locally available game televised by KTBU (channel 55), also will produce Comets content throughout the year. Tegna, the owner of KHOU, also has local broadcasting rights for the Indiana Fever and Dallas Wings in those teams' home markets. "The Comets' return to Houston is a big moment for the city, and we're proud to be part of it," Tegna's senior vice president and head of sports rights Brad Ramsey said. "This partnership expands our WNBA footprint and lets us connect the team with the community, bringing fans closer to the Comets on and off the court, all year." The original Comets were an immediate WNBA dynasty. As one of the first eight franchises when the league tipped off in 1997, the Comets, led by future Basketball Hall of Famers Cynthia Cooper , Sheryl Swoopes and Tina Thompson , won the first four WNBA championships. However, interest waned a decade later and after ownership and arena changes, the Comets folded at the end of 2008 when owner Hilton Koch couldn't find a buyer willing to meet his $10 million price tag to sell the team. The WNBA has experienced a popularity explosion since and Houston Rockets owner Tilman Fertitta agreed to buy the Connecticut Sun for $300 million earlier this year and move them to Houston, rebranding them as the Comets. The team will begin play at Toyota Center in 2027. "Bringing the Comets back to Houston is about reigniting the passion, pride and energy that have always connected this organization with its fans and community," Rockets and Comets president of business operations Gretchen Sheirr said. "As the WNBA continues to reach new heights, we're thrilled to partner with Tegna to make Comets basketball more accessible to fans across the Houston area through free, over-the-air broadcasts on KTBU and additional coverage on KHOU. We're excited to bring fans closer to the action and deliver outstanding coverage as we begin this exciting new chapter in Comets history." Subscribe There’s more to Houston with the Chronicle. item.title: ‘What if He Would’ve Died?’ — Super Bowl Champion Labels Eagles ‘Selfish’ for Mishandling Jalen Hurts’ Blood Clots
item.description: ‘What if He Would’ve Died?’ — Super Bowl Champion Labels Eagles ‘Selfish’ for Mishandling Jalen Hurts’ Blood Clots Leonard Fournette took aim at the Philadelphia Eagles over their handling of Jalen Hurts’ blood clot, with the former NFL running back calling out the team for letting its quarterback play in London after doctors found the clot in his calf. Hurts’ health has become one of the NFL’s biggest storylines since his condition worsened, raising questions about why medical staff cleared him to play and then make the seven-plus-hour flight home after a clot was discovered in his calf. The NFL has defended the Eagles’ medical team, saying its protocols were followed, while the NFL Players Association has called for a full investigation into the care Hurts received. Leonard Fournette Calls Out Medical Staff and Coaches for Allowing Jalen Hurts To Play Fournette, who won Super Bowl LV with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, shared his thoughts on the “4th and South” podcast in a clip the show posted Thursday, making it clear where he believes the fault lies. “This is, to me, selfish on behalf of the Eagles and whoever is representing them on the medical staff,” Fournette said. “What if he would have died?” Despite the heat behind his words, Fournette did offer one caveat. “Or maybe he decided to take it upon himself just to play, right? Being the warrior he is, the gladiator, being there for his team.” BE THE GM OF YOUR FAVORITE TEAM: PFN’s Free NFL Mock Draft Simulator Still, he did not let the people around Hurts off the hook. “If you’re a coach, right, no matter how bad we want to play, you should know, they should know, this is a risk taker with his life. I do not respect the decision at all.” Fournette’s criticism traces back to the Eagles’ Week 5 trip. After a team meeting on Oct. 10, Hurts went to the Cleveland Clinic in London, where he was diagnosed with a superficial blood clot, a person with knowledge of the treatment told Yahoo Sports. item.description: BYU defensive back Matthias Leach (27) reacts to making a defensive stop to end the game during game against Notre Dame, Saturday, Oct. 17, 2026, in Provo, Utah. | Tyler Tate, Associated Press When starting BYU defensive backs Therrian “Tre” Alexander III and Jayven Williams left the game on the same Notre Dame drive toward the end of the third quarter last Saturday, an Irish touchdown seemed somewhat inevitable. For BYU, seldom-used reserves Matthias Leach (a redshirt sophomore) and Jordyn Criss (a redshirt freshman) joined veteran Evan “Schmev” Johnson in the secondary to match up with outstanding Notre Dame receivers Jordan Faison, Micah Gilbert and Jaden Greathouse. Not only did BYU’s patched-together defense rise up and force a field goal on that ND possession, it forced a field goal on the Irish’s next possession when BYU’s fake punt attempt went awry. Alexander returned to the game, but Williams was cramping up and Leach played the remainder of the game, an eventual 28-24 win for BYU. “They knew what I was capable of, and I know what I’m capable of. When I came into the game they let me know, ‘Man, Matthias, you were meant to be here. You’re supposed to be here. Just go have fun.’ That put me in a different mindset.” BYU cornerback Matthias Leach “Super proud of Matthias Leach and how he came in and played,” said BYU defensive coordinator Kelly Poppinga. “I thought he performed really well at the end of the game when those guys went down (and almost scored). item.description: Oscar Piastri believes Red Bull have made significant progress in recent races, describing Max Verstappen's team as the most consistently competitive on the grid. The McLaren driver also highlighted Ferrari's impressive cornering performance, suggesting that the Italian outfit continues to lose valuable time on the straights. Mandatory Credit: Pablo Robles-Imagn Images World Series Storylines Familiar Faces Some faces will be familiar to both teams. The Rays drafted Drew Rasmussen in 2017. However, he opted to return to college, but eventually underwent Tommy John surgery. The Brewers drafted him in 2018, and he made his MLB debut during the shortened 2020 season. The next season, the Brewers traded Rasmussen to the Rays for shortstop Willy Adames . The trade benefited both clubs, but now Rasmussen will take the mound for the team that originally drafted him against the team he broke into the big leagues with. Like Rasmussen, NLCS MVP Jake Bauers was drafted by the Rays and played for them in 2018. After that, he bounced around for a few seasons before finding a home in Milwaukee. Bauers had a breakout season with the Brew Crew, hitting 26 home runs. He has hit some key home runs this postseason and is a big threat the Rays will have to watch. Then there is Freddy Peralta . From 2018-2025, he was one of baseball’s top pitchers, helping the Brewers reach the postseason multiple times. He pitched in several big games for the team, and after the team parted ways with Corbin Burnes , he became their ace. As a pending free agent, the Mets traded Peralta. However, he struggled with the Mets, but the Rays acquired him at the trade deadline , hoping he would regain his form. He did, earning ALCS MVP honors. Rest vs. Rust? The Brewers will be the most rested team in this World Series. After sweeping the Dodgers last Thursday, they’ve had seven days off. The Rays will have had only three days between winning the pennant and Game 1. Rest isn’t always a good thing, though. Teams that sweep their LCS don’t always fare well in the World Series. The latest example of a team sweeping the LCS and losing in the World Series was the 2015 Mets, who swept the Chicago Cubs before falling in five games to the Kansas City Royals. In fact, since the best-of-seven LCS format started in 1985, only two teams have swept the LCS and went on to win the World Series (1995 Atlanta Braves, 2019 Washington Nationals , and 2025 Dodgers). The bullpen has been good at holding leads and keeping deficits at bay. Game 4 of the NLCS is a great example. The Dodgers jumped out to a 4-0 lead after the second inning. However, they did not score another run after that, setting the stage for the Brewers’ comeback win. JoJo Romero and Aaron Ashby combined to throw five shutout innings. The Rays also have strong pitching, but unlike the Brewers, it comes from their rotation. In an era when managers are willing to go to the bullpen as early as possible, manager Kevin Cash takes another approach: letting starters go deep into games. Of course, this is possible because their starting pitching has been so effective. Drew Rasmussen , Peralta, and Nick Martinez have been Cash’s “big three.” This has kept the bullpen fresh and not overused. Perhaps Cash learned his lesson from Game 6 in 2020, when he pulled Blake Snell too early. Writer’s Prediction: The 2026 World Series Champion Pitching wins games in the postseason. The Brewers bullpen has been lights-out and has set the team up to win its first championship. Unless, of course, a fresher bullpen outmatches them. Starting pitching will be the difference maker in this series. We know the Brewers will not hesitate to pull their starter early. The Rays will let their “big three” go deep into games. The Rays’ bullpen will be fresher and, as a result, more effective. It will not be easy to shut down this explosive Brewers lineup, but the Rays will find a way when it matters most. This series will require six games. By the end of the night, the Tampa Bay Rays will be World Series champions for the first time in franchise history. As for the World Series MVP, I think Peralta will become the tenth player to win the LCS and World Series MVP. The Last Word Please comment your World Series predictions below. item.description: This was a momentous night in Bournemouth’s history, although the truth is they would have been given a far sterner examination by Coventry or Hull. The visitors resembled holograms even before Mike Maignan, their goalkeeper, rendered their task impossible with a deserved sending-off in the first half. By then Justin Kluivert had given Bournemouth the lead with a penalty and it was another spot-kick from Marcus Tavernier, given after Maignan’s rush of blood, that underlined their overwhelming superiority. Amine Adli applied the garnish with a late free-kick and it meant an abject return to British shores for Ruben Amorim, who would have been excused seeing this particular week as the opportunity to make a point. item.title: Haiti move Nations League home clash with USA to Miami amid gang violence crisis
item.description: Concacaf approves exceptional hosting arrangement Haiti to face US at Nu Stadium on 14 November Miami’s Haitian community offers home advantage Concacaf on Thursday announced it has approved Haiti’s request to relocate their Nations League quarter-final first leg against the United States on 14 November from Kingston, Jamaica, to Miami in an “exceptional hosting arrangement”. Haiti have been unable to play nominal “home” games within their borders since July 2021, with the United Nations estimating that 90% of the capital of Port-au-Prince – including the national stadium – is controlled by violent gangs. Haiti’s match, the first leg of a home-and-away series against the US, had been booked for Kingston. The Grenadiers played their 2026 World Cup qualifiers in Curaçao, Aruba and Barbados. However, the Nations League format slated Curaçao and Jamaica to host their matches on the same night as Haiti’s, shunting Haiti to Sabina Park, the home of the Jamaica national team until their current venue opened in 1962. Now a cricket ground, Sabina Park hosted two of Haiti’s Nations League qualifiers. Continue reading...

item.title: Trump’s Fifa peace prize was a sham. A reimagined award can still have meaning | Leander Schaerlaeckens
item.description: The first awarding marked the apex of Gianni Infantino’s hubris. A new version could highlight the good in the world of soccer Sign up for our free newsletter here Poor Fifa peace prize. Unloved, unliked, mocked, tainted by association with its first winner. And now demoted, too, after Fifa’s president, Gianni Infantino, dumped the thing on the global governing body’s “social responsibility committee” to look after. To redeem it, rather than to ditch it, to spare Infantino the embarrassment of acknowledging that his fake prize was really just a fake prize all along. Here is where we should probably acknowledge that, as fake prizes go, and in the context of what it was intended to accomplish, the first awarding of the Fifa peace prize was an unqualified success. It achieved exactly what it was meant to, made by Infantino to flatter Donald Trump, the man he needed to keep on his side to safeguard the riches to be extracted from the North American market in order to consolidate his power base within Fifa. Trump, the gullible buffoon, was pleased as punch – handed a big, golden bauble and a medal he placed around his own neck – and briefly forgot about the Nobel peace prize he desperately covets . Leander Schaerlaeckens is the author of The Long Game: US Men’s Soccer and Its Savage, Four-Decade Journey to the Top, or Thereabouts, which is out now . He teaches at Marist University. And then some. It was a tumultuous summer for the Brazil midfielder. A fine World Cup on a personal level was marred by a crucial penalty miss in the last-16 loss against Norway . Now he had the dream move lined up to Arsenal but it could not happen without breaking some hearts at Newcastle. Guimarães admits he lay awake at night as the emotions swirled. How could he leave Newcastle, the club where he made so many connections and enjoyed so many highs after joining from Lyon in January 2022 ? There were the Champions League qualifications and, above all, the Carabao Cup triumph in 2025 that ended a 70-year wait for a domestic trophy. On the other hand, how could he resist Arsenal and the prospect of competing regularly for the game’s top honours? Continue reading...

item.title: Nottingham Forest’s false start places early focus on Glasner and Delap
item.description: Austrian’s tactics need adapting to but Forest are in the bottom three and their owner is not the patient type Sitting 19th in the Premier League was not the plan for Nottingham Forest after the arrival of a highly acclaimed manager and a £45m striker to fuel their ambitions. The fates of Oliver Glasner and Liam Delap are intertwined and with the stark stats of zero home goals and a solitary point at the City Ground it is not the dream start they were aiming for. As Delap prepares to return to Ipswich, where his career ignited, on Friday night, Forest are remaining calm. There is a desperation to get away from the short-termism that caused so many problems; 12 months ago, they were on their third head coach of a disappointing season. This summer they were ruthless with the removal of Vítor Pereira, who had done a fine job to escape the drop, because they saw an opportunity to upgrade with Glasner, hoping he could transform Forest like he did Crystal Palace. They had scaled the Champions League summit on goal difference when Henrik Heggheim put through his own net and the fact was not lost on the Holte End, who reflected their position in song and perhaps allowed themselves another glimpse back to the days when their supremacy was undisputed. “We’ve conquered before, we’re prepared for more,” the pre-match tifo display had read. Perhaps Villa really will rekindle the spirit of 1982 but the frustration here, albeit minor in the wider scheme, was that they could not maintain their bird’s-eye view over the continent. A superbly taken volley by Peter Christiansen, awarded by the video assistant referee after initially being disallowed for offside, gave Viking a consolation their second-half display deserved and meant Unai Emery’s side must make do with slumming it just behind Paris Saint-Germain. item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.title: Too much Overlap? Gary Neville’s podcast empire knows no bounds
item.description: The Overlap has gone daily, with Steven Gerrard and Joe Hart among the latest additions to an ever-growing family Viewed in 2026, Nathan Barley, Chris Morris’s 2005 sitcom, shows remarkable prescience about the last two decades of metropolitan life, from smartphone addiction and digital derangement to sheer existential vapidity. When Barley’s character referred to his occupation as “self-facilitating media node”, Morris and co-writer Charlie Brooker were way ahead on the creator economy. What the pair failed to predict was ex-footballers joining the sector in droves. These days, if you are a former footballer without a podcast or YouTube channel, then did you ever really play the game? Setting aside the Gary Lineker Goalhanger empire, manspreading its centrist-dad agenda into issues way beyond guffaws with Micah Richards and Alan Shearer, there is Gary Neville to rule them all. Manchesterism’s second-most influential practitioner has been on heavy manoeuvres. Unlike Lineker’s productions, the Overlap’s output continues to stick largely to football; a rugby podcast was mothballed in February, though its cricket equivalent continues. Continue reading...

His work here was done, Hansi Flick invited him to take the weight off his feet and his shoulders, not that he wanted to. First, though, he took Lamine Yamal’s head in his hands and, leaning in away from the amateur lip readers, tried to make himself heard over the noise. “I told him I was proud of him because he played a fantastic game,” he said. At least he could think of something. When Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring just nine minutes into the match that was supposed to find out how good Barcelona really were, it hadn’t been easy. Nothing erudite, anyway. On the morning that Barcelona went to Betis – first v third, a proper opponent at last – Jorge Valdano had lamented that sometimes he doesn’t have the words, and he always has the words. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
